title: Bootstrap completion stamp — project-management capability
description: Formal shape of the adopter's `project/bootstrap-stamp.yaml` — the machine-written attestation that `bootstrap` completed in THIS repository, and the input the prerequisite gate every non-exempt pm verb calls reads (#747, enforcing DEC-017's hard-gate role in code). Unlike the sibling adopter files, this one is never hand-edited: `bootstrap` writes it on a clean completion and `migrate` refreshes it, so the schema exists to document the contract and to keep `pkit data validate` clean rather than to guide an author. `additionalProperties: false` is load-bearing for the same reason as the config's: the gate reads the file through defensive access, so an unknown key would be silently ignored. Document-shaped schema: the file IS the resource (no top-level id collection). Companion per COR-018 / COR-023.

binds_to.description: Repo-relative globs matching the adopter-data files this schema validates (COR-023 fallback binding). Present on the kit-shipped binding carrier; absent from adopter data files.

pkit_schema.description: Self-describing adopter-data binding tag, `project-management:bootstrap-stamp` (COR-023). The writer emits it so the file resolves to this schema by field as well as by glob.

bootstrap.description: The attestation itself. Its presence is not sufficient: the gate requires `completed_at` and `capability_version` to be non-empty, so a stub block reads as 'not bootstrapped' rather than as a pass.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the completion this stamp attests.

capability_version.description: The capability version installed when the stamp was written. Makes the stamp a staleness signal rather than a boolean: an upgrade whose bootstrap obligations changed is detectable by comparing this against the installed `package.yaml` version. Staleness is reported, never a refusal on its own.

by.description: Which writer last wrote this stamp. `bootstrap` = the real event. `migrate` = refreshed on a successful migration (migrate never CREATES a stamp — that would let a never-bootstrapped project pass the gate). `migration-grandfather` = written by the capability migration that carried a pre-gate install forward, so the stamp records a PRESUMPTION (the install predates the gate and was in use) rather than an observed bootstrap.

repo.description: The normalised `origin` identity (`host/owner/repo`) of the repository the stamp was written for, or null when no origin could be resolved locally. The stamp lives in the seed-once `project/` subtree, so it can arrive by copy; the gate refuses a stamp naming a DIFFERENT repo than the one it runs in, which makes a copied or seeded stamp inert rather than fail-open. Compared only when both sides resolve — an unresolvable identity never fabricates a refusal.
